title: The Rough Wreck
premise: Tamsin Montrose, a salvage diver who never stays anywhere longer than a contract, is diving a wreck the navy quietly forbids when a dying prospector named Ede Voss trades her a hand-drawn chart for one promise: finish what he started. The map points to the Corvane, a treasure ship that sank with a colonial governor's stolen fortune — and with documents proving the fortune was looted from the very families the navy now protects. Racing a monsoon and a ruthless salvage fleet commanded by Tamsin's estranged former mentor, Captain Ilsa Reyes, Tamsin gathers a ragtag crew who slowly become the family she never let herself have. In the end, Tamsin must choose between keeping the treasure that would free them all and revealing the truth that would destroy Reyes but cost her crew everything; she surfaces with the truth, the monsoon swallows the wreck, and the found family sails on with nothing but each other — and, for the first time, a reason to stop moving.
about_author: Zephyrine Thackeray is the pen name of a former merchant marine radio operator who spent eleven years on salvage crews across the Coral and Andaman seas before trading the deck for a desk. They write adventure novels from a houseboat that moves, on principle, twice a year.

chapters.title: Salt in the Wires
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Diving an unlisted wreck off Kestrel Point, she finds a navy hull plate stamped with a serial that shouldn't exist, and the navy arrives within hours to buy her silence. The beat: unease — the world is bigger and dirtier than she assumed.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wouldn't Sink
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In a port dive bar she patches up Ede Voss, a prospector coughing seawater and blood, who recognizes her name from her mother's old crew. He says her mother died looking for something he found. Beat: a hook she can't ignore.

chapters.title: A Map for a Promise
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Voss trades her the chart of the Corvane for one promise: raise what's in the strongroom before the monsoon, and give the documents inside to the families they were stolen from. He dies by dawn. Beat: a promise made too easily.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She calculates the monsoon window: six tides of safe diving, then nothing. She also learns the navy's salvage fleet is already mobilizing under Captain Ilsa Reyes — the woman who taught her to dive and then testified against her mother. Beat: the clock starts.

chapters.title: Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Tamsin recruits what the port has left: Brannoc, a disgraced engineer; Sefa, a teenage runaway who can read currents; and Ovid, a washed-up archivist who knows the Corvane's manifest. Beat: reluctant assembly, sparks of friction.

chapters.title: The Kestrel's Wake
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. They refit a rotting survey boat, the Kestrel's Wake, with borrowed parts and Brannoc's stubborn genius. Sefa stows a secret of her own aboard. Beat: fragile hope built on rust.

chapters.title: What the Navy Won't Discuss
chapters.summary: Ovid's POV. In the colonial archive, Ovid finds the Corvane's true manifest: not trade goods but the looted treasury of the Meridian families, and a governor's confession sealed inside. Beat: the treasure is evidence — the truth is the prize.

chapters.title: First Tide
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. First dive on the Corvane's outer hull; Tamsin touches the wreck her mother died chasing and comes back shaking. Reyes's scout ship appears on the horizon. Beat: awe braided with dread.

chapters.title: Currents and Lies
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa reads a riptide that nearly kills Tamsin and saves her, earning a place on the crew — but hides that she recognized Reyes's scout from her own past. Beat: trust earned, trust withheld.

chapters.title: The Fleet at Anchor
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Reyes invites Tamsin aboard her flagship under a flag of truce. Over brandy, Reyes offers partnership and warns that the strongroom is a navy matter. Tamsin sees her mentor's ambition has calcified into something colder. Beat: the past offers a deal.

chapters.title: Second Tide
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. The crew cuts into the Corvane's cargo hold and finds it already stripped — someone dove here years ago. Voss's map shows a second, sealed compartment below the waterline. Beat: hope deferred.

chapters.title: Ovid's Confession
chapters.summary: Ovid's POV. Ovid admits he was the archivist who catalogued the looted treasury and stayed silent for thirty years; he joined the crew to atone. The crew's fury nearly breaks them apart. Beat: loyalty vs. truth, first wound.

chapters.title: Storm Signs
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The monsoon shifts early; the window shrinks to four tides. Reyes's fleet begins dredging operations that will collapse the wreck. Beat: the clock accelerates.

chapters.title: Third Tide
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A brutal dive through the flooded lower decks; Tamsin finds her mother's dive knife wedged in a bulkhead, proof she reached the compartment and never left it. Beat: grief made physical.

chapters.title: The Drowned Cabin
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Against orders and safety margins, Tamsin enters the compartment's antechamber and finds a skeleton wearing her mother's rig, one hand still on the strongroom wheel. Beat: the quest becomes personal reckoning.

chapters.title: Mutiny Weather
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Brannoc refuses to let Tamsin dive again on those margins; the crew splits between the promise and survival. Tamsin asserts command for the first time, badly. Beat: leadership's ugly birth.

chapters.title: Reyes's Gambit
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV (first antagonist chapter). Reyes, pressured by a navy minister to make the Corvane vanish before the monsoon, orders the wreck sealed with charges — burying the truth with the treasure. Beat: power chooses silence.

chapters.title: Sefa's Secret
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa reveals she is the granddaughter of a Meridian family the navy ruined; Reyes's scout ship has been hunting her since the port. Her truth re-anchors Ovid's and reframes the crew's mission. Beat: truth as glue.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The crew works the strongroom wheel in relay dives, Brannoc rigging a winch from salvage. They crack the outer seal as Reyes's dredge bites into the reef a quarter-mile away. Beat: exhausted, stubborn hope.

chapters.title: The Minister's Man
chapters.summary: Ovid's POV. A navy liaison offers Ovid rehabilitation and a pension for the manifest's location; Ovid plays along and learns the charges will be laid at the next low tide. Beat: betrayal as intelligence.

chapters.title: The Wheel Turns
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Fifth tide: the strongroom door opens — and inside, instead of gold, they find the documents and a single sealed letter in her mother's hand, addressed to Tamsin. Beat: the treasure was never gold.

chapters.title: The Letter
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In her mother's letter: she found the documents, chose truth over fortune, and was betrayed to Reyes by someone on her own crew. Tamsin realizes the same rot could be aboard the Kestrel's Wake. Beat: paranoia poisons the found family.

chapters.title: Who Told the Navy
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Tamsin interrogates her own crew; accusations fly, Sefa is nearly put off the boat, and Brannoc discovers a transmitter hidden in the engine housing. Beat: the family fractures under suspicion.

chapters.title: The Transmitter
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. The transmitter is old navy issue — planted before they ever left port. It wasn't a crew member; Reyes has been tracking them from the first tide. Beat: relief and horror together.

chapters.title: Reyes Closes In
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes's flagship bears down through building seas. She reflects on Tamsin's mother — the one person who ever chose truth over her — and hardens her resolve to bury the past. Beat: the antagonist's tragic core.

chapters.title: Running the Reef
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. A night chase through the reef maze; Sefa pilots the Kestrel's Wake through channels no chart shows, buying one tide of separation. The crew, bloodied, laughs for the first time. Beat: found family forged in fear.

chapters.title: Last Tide
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The monsoon's leading edge arrives as a black wall. One dive window remains. Tamsin goes down alone to retrieve the documents and her mother's letter, leaving the gold where it lies. Beat: the choice made.

chapters.title: The Charge
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Reyes's demolition team reaches the wreck; Brannoc dives to jam the charges and is caught in the first detonation. The Corvane begins to collapse. Beat: sacrifice without certainty.

chapters.title: Into the Collapse
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin dives into the collapsing wreck to drag Brannoc out, guided by Sefa's shouted current readings and Ovid's memory of the deck plans. Beat: the crew saving each other, literally.

chapters.title: Surface
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. They surface with Brannoc alive, the documents sealed in a brass tube, and the Corvane swallowed by silt and storm. Behind them, Reyes's fleet loses the wreck to the monsoon forever. Beat: grief and triumph in one breath.

chapters.title: The Monsoon
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The Kestrel's Wake runs before the storm, half-flooded, the crew bailing and steering by turns. In the chaos, they are no longer strangers — they are a crew, a family. Beat: unity through survival.

chapters.title: Port of Meridian
chapters.summary: Ovid's POV. They reach the Meridian islands and deliver the documents to the surviving families. The governor's confession detonates politically; the navy minister falls. Beat: truth lands harder than treasure.

chapters.title: Reyes's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes is recalled to face inquiry. Before she goes, she meets Tamsin once more and admits — without apology — that she testified against Tamsin's mother to protect her own command. Beat: the antagonist's truth, unhealed.

chapters.title: What Voss Knew
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Among Voss's effects they find his old log: he was the crew member who betrayed Tamsin's mother, and the map and promise were his penance. Tamsin forgives a dead man she owes everything to. Beat: loyalty vs. truth, resolved.

chapters.title: The Weight of Nothing
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Recovering, broke, the crew faces a choice: sell their story to a syndicate for a fortune, or let the truth stand free. Each chooses, one by one, to walk away from the money. Beat: the theme made choice.

chapters.title: Anchorage
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. For the first time, the Kestrel's Wake stays in one harbor longer than a contract. Sefa enrolls in the Meridian maritime school; Ovid begins writing the true history. Beat: stopping, and finding it costs less.

chapters.title: The Navy's Silence
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A navy offer arrives: salvage rights, a pardon, a commission — in exchange for never publishing Ovid's history. Tamsin burns the letter on the beach. Beat: power's last corruption, refused.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin dives the reef one last time — not for salvage, but to lay her mother's knife to rest in the open water where the Corvane sleeps. Beat: grief given a grave.

chapters.title: Six Tides, Kept
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. One year later: the Kestrel's Wake, refitted and renamed, takes a legitimate contract. The crew argues about dinner, not survival. Tamsin realizes she has stopped moving — and stayed. Beat: the promise fulfilled, the family kept.

chapters.title: The Rough Wreck
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, closing. Standing watch at dawn, Tamsin logs their position and writes one line in the logbook: 'Some wrecks are meant to be raised; some are meant to be remembered.' The monsoon season ends; the horizon is clear. Beat: quiet, earned peace.
